summary: This standards-track RFC defines a new RTCP Extended Report block for reporting loss concealment metrics for video applications of RTP.

plainLanguage.summary: A report card on how well a video player hid missing pieces so you did not notice.

questions: what is frame freeze in video
subtitle: A new RTCP report that tells monitors how much video was damaged by packet loss and how the receiver patched it up.

tldr.problem: Video receivers hide the effects of packet loss with concealment tricks, but monitors upstream cannot see which losses happened or which tricks the receiver used, so they cannot judge the quality users actually saw.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7867 defines an RTCP Extended Report block, block type 34, that carries durations and proportions of impaired and concealed video, and a rule for reporting frame freezes separately from other concealment methods.
tldr.outcome: Senders and monitoring systems, such as an IPTV management system, can estimate the quality of experience of video without looking at the picture itself. It is a Proposed Standard and nothing obsoletes it.

today: RFC 7867 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2016, and no later RFC obsoletes or updates it. It is the definition of the video loss concealment XR block.

sections.title: Why Report Loss Concealment
sections.content:
Packets get lost in IP networks, so video decoders use loss concealment, a range of techniques that mask the effects of that loss. RFC 7867 defines one new RTCP Extended Report (XR) block so that a receiver can report how much concealment it applied.

The motivation is quality monitoring. A video probe placed upstream of the endpoint may not see loss that happens between the probe and the endpoint, and may not know which concealment method the endpoint is using at that moment. Receiver reports give monitors and senders that missing view of the Quality of Experience (QoE).

The block adds to the audio concealment blocks of RFC 7294 and the extended report framework of RFC 3611. Its metrics belong to the class of transport-related terminal metrics from RFC 6792.
sections.plainLanguage: Imagine a teacher who cannot see your screen but wants to know how smooth your video looked. You tell the teacher how often it glitched and how you patched it. That is what this report does.

sections.title: Four Kinds of Video Loss Concealment
sections.content:
The RFC sorts concealment into four types:

  • Frame freeze: the damaged frame is not shown, and the previously displayed frame stays on screen for the length of the loss event.
  • Interframe extrapolation: the same area from earlier frames is used to guess the missing pixels. It works well in a scene with no motion but is very noticeable with significant movement. It may also give poor results for frames such as IDR frames that depend on no other frame.
  • Interpolation: undamaged pixels in the same frame are used to estimate the missing block.
  • Error-resilient encoding: the sender adds redundancy, either inside the compressed bitstream or at the bitstream level, for example Forward Error Correction (FEC), so the receiver can correct errors.

Methods b, c and d are usually deployed together in complex decoders, while frame freeze is relatively independent and may be used in simple decoders. Frame freeze repairs whole frames, whereas the others repair finer elements such as macroblocks or bitstreams, so their metrics differ slightly. That is why the report treats frame freeze and the other three methods as two cases.
sections.plainLanguage: If a page of a flip book is torn, you can keep showing the last page, copy the neighbouring drawing, or have a spare copy ready. These are the same kinds of tricks a video player uses.

sections.title: The Video Loss Concealment Report Block
sections.content:
The block is identified by block type BT=34. It MUST be sent together with the Measurement Information Block of RFC 6776, which supplies the measurement period. If that period does not arrive in the same compound RTCP packet, the receiver MUST discard the block. The metrics are typically measured when a frame is decoded and rendered for playout.

The header fields are:

  • I (2 bits): 10 means interval, 11 cumulative, 01 sampled (MUST NOT be used for this block) and 00 is reserved.
  • V (2 bits): 10 means frame freeze and 11 means another concealment method. 01 and 00 are reserved. If both are used for a stream, two blocks SHOULD be compounded together.
  • RSV (4 bits): reserved, set to zero by senders and ignored by receivers.
  • Block Length (16 bits): MUST be 5 when V=10 and 4 when V=11; a block with any other length MUST be discarded.
  • SSRC of Source (32 bits): as defined in RFC 3611.

The body carries the durations Impaired Duration and Concealed Duration, both 32 bits in RTP timestamp units. The value 0xFFFFFFFE means out of range and 0xFFFFFFFF means the measurement is unavailable. The optional Mean Frame-Freeze Duration exists only when V=10. Four 8-bit fields follow: MIFP, MCFP, FFSC and a reserved byte.
sections.plainLanguage: The report is a small form with boxes to fill in. One box says what kind of patching was used, others say how long the video was broken and how long it was patched, and a few more give percentages.

sections.title: How the Proportions Are Calculated
sections.content:
Three 8-bit fields are fixed-point numbers with the binary point at the left edge of the field. Each is computed by dividing a count, then multiplying by 256, limiting the maximum value to 255 to avoid overflow, and taking the integer part.

  • MIFP (Mean Impaired Frame Proportion): per frame, missing macroblocks divided by total macroblocks, averaged over the frames in the period. A frame that is totally lost SHOULD count as 0xFF.
  • MCFP (Mean Concealed Frame Proportion): the same idea using concealed macroblocks. A totally concealed lost frame SHOULD count as 0xFF, and a frame with no concealed macroblocks SHOULD count as 0. For V=10, every frame during a freeze counts as totally concealed, so 0xFF MUST be assigned.
  • FFSC (Fraction of Frames Subject to Concealment): frames that had concealment applied divided by all frames. A value of 0 means no concealed frames and 0xFF means every frame in the interval was concealed.

The Mean Frame-Freeze Duration is the total duration of all freeze events divided by the number of events. Appendix A restates all six metrics in the template of RFC 6390.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of saying a long number, the report squeezes each percentage into one small number from 0 to 255, where 255 means all of it.

sections.title: Signalling the Block in SDP
sections.content:
Use of RTCP XR blocks is signalled with the Session Description Protocol, as defined in RFC 3611. This RFC adds one value to the rtcp-xr attribute: xr-vlc-block = "vlc", added to the xr-format rule.

In an offer/answer exchange, the usage for unilateral rtcp-xr parameters in Section 5.2 of RFC 3611 applies unchanged.
sections.plainLanguage: Before the call, each side says in its setup message that it can send this report, using the short word vlc.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The block is believed to add no security considerations beyond those of RFC 3611. It carries no per-packet statistics, so the confidentiality risk noted there does not apply.

The remaining risk is false data. An attacker is likely to put incorrect information in the reports, which would distort the estimate of concealment performance and user QoE. Where security matters, implementations SHOULD apply encryption and authentication to the block, following RFC 7202. One way is the AVPF profile with the Secure RTP profile (SAVPF, RFC 5124), though other mechanisms from RFC 7201 may suit better.
sections.plainLanguage: Someone could write a fake report card and make the video look better or worse than it was. Locking the reports so only the real player can write them prevents that.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA is asked to assign block type value 34 to the Video Loss Concealment Metric Report Block in the RTCP XR Block Type Registry. The RFC also registers a new parameter, video-loss-concealment, in the RTCP XR SDP Parameters Registry. The contact for the registrations is the RAI Area Directors.
sections.plainLanguage: The block gets its own official number, 34, so nobody else uses it for something different.

fields.name: I
fields.desc: Interval, cumulative or sampled metric flag.

fields.name: Impaired Duration
fields.desc: Video impaired by loss before any concealment.

fields.name: FFSC
fields.desc: Fraction of frames subject to concealment.

items.label: Frame-freeze
items.desc: Last good frame is held; Block Length is 5.

items.label: Other method
items.desc: Extrapolation, interpolation or error-resilient encoding; Block Length is 4.
